label: rem:periodic-table-demand
title: The valley of stability is the demand-minimizing locus in $(Z, N)$-space
html:
Conjecture. For each mass number A = Z + N, the experimentally observed stable isotope (Z_*, N_*) is the unique minimizer of the demand magnitude:

  (Z_*, N_*)
  =
  \arg\min_{Z + N = A}
  |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z, N))|

where \mathcal{A}(Z, N) is the derived atom (derived atom) and |\mathrm{dem}| is the demand magnitude (demand stability).

Formal statement

Let \mathcal{V} \subset \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2 be the set of pairs (Z, N) such that \mathcal{A}(Z, N) minimizes demand at fixed A:

  \mathcal{V}
  =
  \left\{
    (Z, N) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^2
    :
    |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z, N))|
    \leq
    |\mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}(Z', N'))|
    \text{ for all } Z' + N' = Z + N
  \right\}.

Conjecture. \mathcal{V} coincides with the experimentally observed valley of stability for all A \leq 238.

Subsidiary conjectures

(i) Magic numbers from demand closure. The nuclear magic numbers \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} are the values of Z (or N) at which the nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) achieves demand closure \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{N}) = \varnothing for at least one value of the complementary quantum number.

(ii) Shell closure from electron demand. The atomic noble gases (Z = 2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86) are the values of Z at which the atom \mathcal{A}(Z, N_*) achieves \mathrm{dem}(\mathcal{A}) = \varnothing for the most abundant stable isotope N_*.

(iii) Drip lines from Layer-2 binomial dissociation. Microscopic braid reduction (Unique nuclear normal form via Gröbner reduction in H_n(q)) terminates with a finite normal form for every braid word. The proton and neutron drip lines arise instead in the macroscopic toric layer (Physical cluster chamber, drip-line monomer reduction, and the Hoyle triple-alpha bottleneck): crossing the drip wall flips the binomial orientation x_{(Z, N \pm 1)} \to x_{(Z, N)} x_{p/n}, so the normal form ceases to be a connected degree-1 nuclide monomial (LP-confined element of H_3(q)) and reduces to a disconnected product x_{\mathrm{core}} x_{p/n}^k (or exceeds the finite hole capacity u_s + w_s = C_s of the active Mayer--Jensen shells).

Inductive verification

This conjecture is verified computationally by inductive Gröbner--Shirshov reduction (derived atom). For each A:

  1. Compute \mathcal{A}(Z, A - Z) for all 0 \leq Z \leq A.
  2. Evaluate |\mathrm{dem}| for each.
  3. Check that the minimizer matches the known stable isotope(s).

The inductive reduction ensures polynomial scaling. Each new nucleon multiplies a bounded-size normal form element by a typed crossing and reduces. For A \leq 12, this is computationally tractable. For A > 12, the transfer matrix identities C_{pp}^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} C_{pp} + \mathbf{1} and C_{nn}^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} C_{nn} + \mathbf{1} compress the calculation.

Predicted vs observed for A \leq 4

A Predicted (Z_*, N_*) Observed \vert \mathrm{dem}_*\vert
1 (1, 0) {}^1\mathrm{H} 0.024
2 (1, 1) {}^2\mathrm{H} 0.058
3 (2, 1) {}^3\mathrm{He} 0.000
4 (2, 2) {}^4\mathrm{He} 0.098

He-3 achieves exact demand closure (|\mathrm{dem}| = 0). He-4 has nonzero demand but minimal Markov trace. The doubly magic stability of He-4 arises from action minimization, not demand closure.
